mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return distribution in declining FEDFUNDS periods shows no significant positive bias (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0% (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent 1-month decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% indicates weakening demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict negative returns (Rank IC < 0.03) or the return distribution in triggered periods shows no significant negative bias (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), weak labor market conditions suppress consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns in high-unemployment periods (UNRATE > 5.0%) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the return distribution matches the baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production (INDPRO) growth relative to its 6-month average signals robust manufacturing output, supporting corporate profit growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The INDPRO growth signal fails to generate positive returns (Rank IC < 0.05) or the return distribution in high INDPRO periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly job growth (PAYEMS) falls below 0.5%, it indicates labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending power, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances with PAYEMS growth < 0.5% (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) and GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 0.3% indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 decline > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and GDPC1 fails to predict negative returns (Rank IC < 0.03) or the return distribution in triggered periods shows no significant negative bias (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized), central bank policy tightening reduces equity valuation multiples, generating negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns in high-inflation periods (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the return distribution matches the baseline.
